findings.name: Unsafe path join in read_avatar() permits path traversal when wired to user input
findings.description: If `read_avatar()` is ever called with request data, an attacker can read any file the process can access — `os.path.join("/srv/avatars", user)` is opened with no normalization or containment check, so an absolute path or "../" sequence escapes the avatar directory. No caller exists in the repo today, so the sink is latent: fixing it is cheap hardening rather than a merge blocker.
findings.attackScript: grep -rn read_avatar → only the definition at src/app/helpers.py:8; no callers.

findings.name: SQL injection in /search via string-concatenated LIKE pattern
findings.description: Any unauthenticated caller of GET /search can read arbitrary data from app.db (e.g. password column) by breaking out of the quoted LIKE literal with a UNION/subselect. The raw `q` query parameter is concatenated directly into the SQL string at line 37 with no sanitization; `limit` is clamped by page_size() and is not tainted.
findings.attackScript: q = request.args.get("q","") (routes.py:34) → cur.execute("SELECT name FROM users WHERE name LIKE '%" + q + "%' LIMIT " + str(limit)) (routes.py:37); e.g. q=' UNION SELECT password FROM users--

findings.name: Unauthenticated OS command injection in /ping (shell=True with query param)
findings.description: Any unauthenticated caller can run arbitrary shell commands as the web process: `GET /ping?host=127.0.0.1;id`. The `host` query parameter is concatenated straight into a shell string passed to `subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True)`, with no validation, allowlist, or auth decorator between the request and the sink. Deployment exposure of the endpoint was not verified.
